valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E. Non-GAAP diluted EPS FY2026 $13.27 (GAAP $12.32) grown per management's FY2027 outlook (adjusted EPS growth low double digits to low teens; secondary-source wording). At the 12-month target date (Nov 2027) an investor prices FY2028 EPS, so target = FY2028 EPS x P/E. USD listing, no FX or ADR conversion.

bear.driver: Consumer spending slowdown, regulatory/interchange settlement pressure and higher litigation/opex; EPS growth 9% in FY2027 and 8% in FY2028

base.driver: Low-double-digit net revenue growth and about 12% EPS growth in both FY2027 and FY2028, value-added services growth in the low-to-mid 20s percent

bull.driver: Cross-border and value-added services outperform, 14% EPS growth in FY2027 and FY2028 with agentic commerce upside

valuation.implied_by_close: At base FY2027 EPS $14.86 the close implies 28.7x (32.1x FY2026 EPS $13.27); the single sourced analyst target of $450 implies 27.1x on base FY2028 EPS, or EPS $17.65 at 25.5x (6.3% above model)
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $16.60 (about 3.9 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: Net revenue growth and non-GAAP EPS growth versus the low-double-digit FY2027 outlook, plus value-added services growth
valuation.next_disclosure: Fiscal Q1 2027 results, expected late January 2027 (date not confirmed)

analyst_notes: Only one named analyst call could be sourced (TD Cowen's Bryan Bergin, target $420 to $450, Buy, after the Oct 27 results), and its 12-month horizon is undocumented so it is excluded from the weighted target. Search snippets also listed Morgan Stanley ($416 to $471), Oppenheimer ($403 to $440), Cantor ($445, Overweight), Susquehanna ($427 to $480) and Bernstein ($475 to $486), but analyst names and dates could not be verified, so they are omitted. The $450 target implies about 27.1x base FY2028 EPS versus the 25.5x base multiple, a gap of 6.3% in EPS or about 1.6 turns.
